site.name: Macedonian Corpus
site.tagline: A searchable corpus of Macedonian with morphological and syntactic annotation

home.title: Corpus of Macedonian Language
home.subtitle: Search word forms, lemmas, part-of-speech tags and syntactic relations

text.title: Word or lemma
text.summary: Search the corpus for a word form or a dictionary form.
text.description: Enter one word. The search matches a token whose written form or whose lemma is that word, so "убаво" also finds "поубаво", whose lemma it is. Metadata such as genre, dialect or speaker get their own filter.
text.partialHint: Off: finds the word form or lemma itself. On: also finds it inside longer words.

lemma.title: Lemma
lemma.description: Search tokens by lemma, i.e. basic or dictionary form of the word. Nouns are usually given in sg.nom (e.g. slovo 'word'), adjectives in m.sg.nom (e.g. nov 'new'), verbs in 1sg.prs (e.g. stana 'stand up').

tag.title: PoS Tag
tag.summary: Search tokens by tags reflecting part-of-speech category and morphological properties.
tag.descriptionOneAfter: standard with minor modifications. The information is provided by a string of characters, reflecting the part-of-speech category (capital) and information marked by the inflection.
tag.descriptionTwo: The strings are specific for each part-of-speech category. For example, slovesa 'words' would be annotated as Nnpn, denoting category as noun and inflection (neutral gender, plural number, default/nominative case, not animated).
tag.descriptionThree: It is possible to search for a full tag and for a part: for example, the query N will find all the nouns and the query Nf all the feminine nouns. You can replace a category tag with ? to get any value, e.g. N?sny will return singular animate nouns in nominative of all genders.

ud.title: UD Tag
ud.descriptionOneBefore: Each sentence is syntactically annotated by the
ud.descriptionOneAfter: standard. Each token is given an ID according to the position in the sentence.
ud.descriptionTwo: For each token, a dependency on other elements within the sentence is declared by these IDs, as well as by the character of the dependency.
ud.descriptionThree: One token in each sentence is marked as its root, usually representing the most verbal element.

udTags.fixed: fixed: element of multiple word expression
udTags.nsubj: nsubj: subject of the main sentence
